content: ## Metadata_Start ## code: en ## title: Custom Component Scenario ## slug: vt-custom-component-scenario ## seoTitle: Custom Component Scenario ## description: ## contentType: Markdown ## Metadata_End 1. Create a Lightning Component using the Developer Console. ![Custom Component Scenario_1](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Custom%20Component%20Scenario_1.png){height="" width=""} 3. Add a {{variable.Field_CustComponentScen_Name}}, select "Lightning Page" and "Lightning Record Page" in the Component Configuration section, and click **Submit**. ![Custom Component Scenario_2](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Custom%20Component%20Scenario_2.png){height="" width=""} 5. In the .cmp, add the following code, but replace the recordId and parentId with IDs from your org. **{{variable.Component_BTPayVirtualTerminal}} Custom Component Sample** ``` ` ` ``` 4. Add a controller.js file if you would like to add an event handler. **Controller.js** ``` `({ handleEvent : function(component, event, helper) { var success = event.getParam("success"); var errorMessage = event.getParam("errorMessage"); var transactionId = event.getParam("transactionId"); console.log (' success ' , success); console.log (' errorMessage ' , errorMessage); console.log (' transactionId ' , transactionId); } })` ``` :::(Info) (NOTE) Adding a javascript file like the one above can allow customers to pass in variables that can be used in flows to meet the needs of a business requirement. ::: 5. Save your file. 6. Navigate to the record page where you want this custom component to live. (ex: Invoice) 7. Use the page editor to drag your custom component onto the page. ![Custom Component Scenario_3](https://cdn.document360.io/f977eec0-500f-40a3-b663-724a51f78075/Images/Documentation/Custom%20Component%20Scenario_3.png){height="" width=""} 8. Click {{variable.Button_Save}}. Now you'll have more flexibility when using your own custom component.
